title: Instance-optimal outer approximation of convex polytopes
formal: Editorial finite-input variant: for every fixed \(d\ge2\), is there a deterministic algorithm which, given a full-dimensional polytope \(K\subseteq B_2^d\) by N vertices and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), constructs a polytope P with \[K\subseteq P\subseteq K+\varepsilon B_2^d,\qquad f(P)\le C_d\operatorname{OPT}(K,\varepsilon),\] in time polynomial in N and 1/epsilon? Here f counts facets and C_d depends only on dimension.
definitions:
The input points have real coordinates, K is their convex hull, and B_2^d is the closed Euclidean unit ball centered at zero. The input promise is compactness, nonempty interior and containment in that ball; no lower bound on its inradius or minimum width is imposed. The Minkowski sum K+epsilon B consists of all x+epsilon u with x∈K and norm(u)≤1. For an outer approximation this containment is equivalent to a Hausdorff error at most epsilon.

OPT(K,epsilon) is the minimum number of facets among all bounded full-dimensional real polytopes Q with K⊆Q⊆K+epsilon B. Its comparator is allowed arbitrary real coefficients, not only input supporting hyperplanes. The algorithm outputs P as a finite list of real linear inequalities; redundant inequalities may be present but their number must also be at most C_d OPT. Facet count alone cannot hide an exponentially large output list. Use the exact-real RAM with +, −, ×, ÷, square roots, comparisons and memory operations at unit cost. All work and output writes are charged; there is no free convex-body optimization oracle. The algorithm, degree of its polynomial bound and approximation constant may depend on fixed d, but not K, N or epsilon.

Choosing a finite vertex representation, a unit-radius normalization and polynomial dependence on 1/epsilon is an editorial specialization of the source’s broad request for an efficient instance-optimal construction. It does not claim polynomial bit complexity or an algorithm for arbitrary oracle-given convex bodies.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete Lean-checked construction with both containments, the instance-by-instance constant-factor output bound and the stated arithmetic time, or prove impossibility in this selected model. Bounds tight only for the worst body of a given volume or diameter do not establish the comparison with OPT for each input. An assumption-based hardness result must remain explicitly conditional.
context:
Arya and Mount give volume-sensitive bounds for outer approximation and distinguish these from the optimal size for an individual body. Their conclusion poses efficient constant-factor instance optimality as a further question.

This card selects a concrete vertex-input algorithmic version. Thin polytopes remain included, so a guarantee depending on a hidden fatness parameter would not suffice.
why: Instance-optimal approximation would adapt representation size to the geometry of the particular polytope.

import_provenance.original_title: Instance-optimal outer approximation of convex polytopes
import_provenance.original_statement: For fixed dimension d, can one efficiently construct an outer polytope P with K⊆P⊆K+εB whose number of facets is within a dimension-dependent constant factor of the minimum possible for that particular input polytope K and error ε? Arya and Mount explicitly distinguish this instance-optimal goal from their achieved volume-sensitive worst-case bounds.

sentences: A convex polytope is approximated from outside within a prescribed Euclidean error.
The goal is to use only a constant factor more facets than the best approximation of that particular input.
The constant may depend on fixed dimension but not shape or accuracy.
Volume-sensitive worst-case bounds do not alone give instance optimality.
The editorial variant fixes real vertex input and polynomial arithmetic time in input size and inverse accuracy.
